name: Weave on a frame loom
blurb: A simple frame loom teaches the whole logic of woven cloth in an afternoon, and produces wall hangings and small rugs while you learn.
gear: A frame loom, or a picture frame with nails
Assorted weft yarns, a shed stick and a tapestry needle
steps: Warp the loom under even tension. Uneven warp tension causes every problem that follows.
Learn the plain weave: over, under, alternating each row.
Learn to leave the weft slack in an arc before beating it down, so the edges do not pull in.
Beat each row down firmly and evenly with a comb or fork.
Learn a texture technique: rya knots for fringe, or soumak for a raised braid.
Finish by tying off the warp and hanging or hemming the piece.
tips: Pulled-in edges — a waist in the middle of the weaving — mean you are pulling the weft tight. Arc it.
Choose a warp strong enough to survive tension. Snapped warp threads mid-project are hard to fix.
proof: A finished woven piece with straight, parallel edges and even beat.
